The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 83 from AD Mathews, complemented by a commanding 133-run stand between FDM Karunaratne and AD Mathews that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.12 RPO. New Zealand's bowling response was spearheaded by Tim Southee (6/68), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 282/10 (89.6 ov), Sri Lanka posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, Sri Lanka sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. BKG Mendis anchored the innings with a resolute 141, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. Tim Southee (2/52) maintained tight lines for New Zealand, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Sri Lanka's total of 287/3 (114.6 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

New Zealand replied strongly with 578, powered by Tom Latham's commanding century (264) to swing the contest. summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Basin Reserve commenced with high tactical intensity as Sri Lanka posted 282/10 (89.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 578/10 (157.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Tom Latham 264 (490b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Tom Latham delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (264 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 53%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, New Zealand faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by AD Mathews (203 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While New Zealand produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
